newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek stocks end with gains, seen consolidating.
newsitem.headline: Greek stocks end with gains, seen consolidating.

text.p: Greek stocks closed 0.67 percent higher with trading volume still at low levels today with no let up on the farmers' strike and brokers not expecting any significant change on Thursday.

"The general index rose because of the good performance of the banking sector", said broker Iakovos Diamantopoulos, of Hermes Brokerage. "Volume was very low and was boosted to over 5 billion drachmas by block trades", he added.
Farmers continued a 14-day blockade of major highways and road links protesting against Greece's austere 1997 budget and vowing to spend the Christmas holidays by the roadblocks.
They were demanding lower diesel fuel prices, cuts in the VAT tax on farm equipment, rescheduling of the debts by farm cooperatives to state banks and higher price supports especially for cotton.
Talks between the socialist government and representatives of the farmers broke down on Wednesday leading to a deadlock.
Prime Minister Costas Simitis refused once more to bow to farmers' demands yesterday, after a cabinet meeting.

The Athens general share index closed up 0.67 percent or 6.04 points higher at 909.34 from Tuesday's 903.30 close after opening at 903.31. Turnover rose to 5.46 billion drachmas on volume of 2.6 million shares.
There were a couple of block trades in Papastratos and Viohalco.
Gainers led losers 96 to 86 with 33 issues unchanged on 215 traded. Banks rose 0.91 percent, industrials gained 0.46 percent with construction slipping 0.07 percent. Small-caps lost 0.31 percent.
